title: Closed orbit maps on spaces with disjoint clopen components
statement: Let $X,Z$ be sober topological spaces, meaning that each nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. Assume each space is the disjoint union of its finitely many irreducible components, all of which are open and closed [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ by homeomorphisms. Let $q:X\to Z$ be continuous, surjective, closed (the image of every closed set is closed), and invariant: $q(hx)=q(x)$. Suppose $q(x)=q(y)$ if and only if $y=hx$ for some $h\in H$. For an orbit $O$ of components of $X$, set $T_O=\bigcup_{C\in O}C$. Then $q^{-1}(q(T_O))=T_O$, $q(T_O)$ is open and closed, and $q(T_O)=q(C)$ for every $C\in O$. Each such image is exactly one irreducible component of $Z$, and $O\mapsto q(T_O)$ is a bijection onto the components of $Z$. If $\eta_C$ is the generic point of $C$, then $q(\eta_C)$ is the generic point of $q(C)$, and $\{h:h\eta_C=\eta_C\}=\{h:hC=C\}$. Empty spaces are allowed.

source.place: Agent topological consequence of Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components) and Tag 004X (definition-generic-point), for closed orbit maps; applied to the point quotient of groupoids.tex Tag 03BL (lemma-points).

proof.text: Every $h\in H$ permutes the components. Indeed, if $hC$ is the union of two relatively closed subsets, their inverse images under $h$ give a closed decomposition of $C$, so one is all of $hC$. If an irreducible subset $E$ contains $hC$, the same argument for $h^{-1}$ makes $h^{-1}E$ irreducible and containing $C$; maximality gives $h^{-1}E=C$. Thus $hC$ is a maximal irreducible subset, using [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components); elementary closed-cover and inverse-homeomorphism argument.

proof.text: Fix a component orbit $O$ and $C\in O$. Invariance and bijectivity of $h$ give $q(hC)=q(C)$, so $q(T_O)=q(C)$. The union $T_O$ is $H$-stable. If $x\in q^{-1}(q(T_O))$, choose $t\in T_O$ with $q(x)=q(t)$; the fibre hypothesis gives $x=ht$ for some $h\in H$, hence $x\in T_O$. The reverse inclusion holds for every map, proving $q^{-1}(q(T_O))=T_O$.

source.place: Elementary set-theoretic argument from the assumed invariant point-orbit fibres; compare groupoids.tex Tag 03BL (lemma-points), whose conclusion is a hypothesis here.

proof.text: The finitely many clopen components make $T_O$ clopen: it is a finite union of closed sets and a union of open sets. Since $q$ is closed, both $q(T_O)$ and $q(X\setminus T_O)$ are closed. Saturation from Step 2 makes these images disjoint, and surjectivity makes their union $Z$. Thus $Z\setminus q(T_O)=q(X\setminus T_O)$ is closed, so $q(T_O)$ is open as well.

source.place: Elementary finite-union, complement, and closed-map argument.

proof.text: Write $B_O=q(T_O)=q(C)$. It is nonempty since $C$ is nonempty. If $B_O=F_1\cup F_2$ with $F_i$ relatively closed, then $C=(q|_C)^{-1}F_1\cup(q|_C)^{-1}F_2$ is a relatively closed decomposition by continuity. Irreducibility of $C$ forces one inverse image to equal $C$, and surjectivity of $q|_C:C\to q(C)$ gives $F_i=B_O$. Therefore $B_O$ is irreducible by [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components); the closed-cover calculation in lemma-image-irreducible-space, written out rather than used as a black box.

proof.text: The nonempty clopen sets $B_O$ form a disjoint partition of $Z$: surjectivity gives the cover, and a point in two images would lift into both orbit unions by Step 2, forcing the orbits equal. Any irreducible subset $E$ meeting $B_O$ lies in $B_O$, since $E=(E\cap B_O)\cup(E\cap(Z\setminus B_O))$ is a relatively closed decomposition with first term nonempty. Thus no irreducible subset properly contains $B_O$, so it is a component. Conversely, any component $D$ has a point in some $B_O$, hence $D\subseteq B_O$ and maximality gives equality. The nonempty disjoint images distinguish the orbits. This proves the required bijection using [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components); direct maximality argument for a clopen irreducible partition.

proof.text: By sobriety choose the generic point $\eta_C$ of $C$, so $\overline{\{\eta_C\}}=C$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. The closed set $q(C)=B_O$ contains $q(\eta_C)$, so $\overline{\{q(\eta_C)\}}\subseteq q(C)$. If $F\subseteq Z$ is any closed set containing $q(\eta_C)$, its closed inverse image contains $\eta_C$, hence contains $C$; thus $q(C)\subseteq F$. Intersecting all such $F$ proves $q(C)=\overline{\{q(\eta_C)\}}$. This is the required generic-point assertion.

source.place: Tag 004X (definition-generic-point), parts (1) and (4); elementary characterization of closure by closed supersets.

proof.text: For a homeomorphism $h$, the closed set $hC$ contains $h\eta_C$, so $\overline{\{h\eta_C\}}\subseteq hC$. Conversely the inverse image of $\overline{\{h\eta_C\}}$ under $h$ is closed and contains $\eta_C$, hence contains $C$; therefore $hC\subseteq\overline{\{h\eta_C\}}$. Thus $h\eta_C$ is generic for $hC$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. If $h\eta_C=\eta_C$, their closures give $hC=C$. If $hC=C$, uniqueness of the generic point in the sober space $X$ gives $h\eta_C=\eta_C$. The two stabilizers are equal. If $X$ is empty, surjectivity forces $Z$ empty; both component sets are empty and every assertion about a component is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 004X (definition-generic-point), parts (1) and (4); elementary closed-set calculation and the stated sobriety hypothesis.
